Name: Bar Leone
Location: 11-15 Bridges Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Italian aperitivo-style cocktail bar, known for its martini and fig-leaf negroni. Walk-in only. Why: Retained Asia's top Hong Kong bar and a high world ranking in 2026 (Asia's 50 Best Bars No. 3 per Epicure Asia); queue forms early.

Name: Argo
Location: G/F, Four Seasons Hotel Hong Kong, 8 Finance Street, Central, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Hotel bar led by an extensive Middle East-inflected spirits list; on the 2026 World's 50 Best Bars list. Why: A hotel-bar splurge, open to 1am (2am Fri/Sat) per Time Out and Cathay; in a hotel, so likely open on Christmas.

Name: COA
Location: Shop A, LG/F, Wah Shin House, 6-10 Shin Hing Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Agave-spirits bar with 200+ mezcals and tequilas and a 41-page agave menu, down steps off Hollywood Road. Why: Long-running regional leader (Asia's best bar 2021); sustained presence on the 2026 Asia's 50 Best list at No. 24.

Name: The Opposites
Location: LG/F, Hilltop Plaza, 49 Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Cocktail bar by Antonio Lai and Samuel Kwok whose playful twin-version drinks climbed 26 places to No. 54 on the extended 2026 list. Why: Fresh Asia's 50 Best (51-100) result, July 2026.

Name: Lan Kwai Fong, SoHo and Peel Street
Location: Lan Kwai Fong, D'Aguilar Street area, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Hong Kong's classic bar-and-club lanes, with SoHo's restaurant-bar strip up the Escalator. Why: Christmas Eve and nights around it are traditionally rowdy street parties here; Christmas night is busy. Official 2026 event details were not found.

Name: Lan Fong Yuen
Location: 2 Gage Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Cha chaan teng credited with silk-stocking milk tea (1952) and said to have started yuenyeung; takeout line moves fast. Why: Origin-story milk tea shop; hours listed Mon-Sat 07:30-18:00 with Sunday closed (possibly outdated).

Name: On The Hill Coffee Bar (Tai Kwun)
Location: Tai Kwun, 10 Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Local specialty coffee brand roasting its own beans, with a bar inside the Tai Kwun heritage compound (the former Central Police Station). Why: Home-grown roaster (not a chain import) in a heritage courtyard, convenient for a coffee between Tai Kwun, PMQ and Hollywood Road.

Name: My Little Coffee Roastery
Location: G/F, 120 Tai Nan Street, Prince Edward, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Small in-house roastery and coffee counter on Tai Nan Street, on the Sham Shui Po / Prince Edward border. Why: Local micro-roaster close to the Sham Shui Po fabric and cafe streets; good for a quiet cup away from tourist cafes.

Name: Introvert Coffee & Roastery
Location: Shop 132A, Ki Lung Street, Sham Shui Po, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Sham Shui Po specialty cafe that roasts its own beans, in the district's cafe-and-craft streets. Why: Indie roaster in Sham Shui Po, easy to combine with the fabric and craft streets and Apliu Street.

Name: OZONE (Ritz-Carlton Hong Kong)
Location: 118/F, The Ritz-Carlton, International Commerce Centre, 1 Austin Road West, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Bar on the 118th floor of ICC billed as the world's highest, with a glass-shielded terrace over Victoria Harbour and the Island skyline. Cocktails with Asian twists, plus a champagne Sunday brunch. Why: The dramatic skyline-from-above bar; locally a special-occasion pick. Reserve a window for dusk (sunset about 17:46) and note the smart-casual dress code.

Name: Kowloon Taproom
Location: G/F, 17-19 Ashley Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: TST bar built around Hong Kong craft beer on rotating taps; local pours have included Hong Kong Beer Co and Lion Rock Brewery. Why: Handy local-craft-beer stop on Ashley Road after the harbourfront. Tap lists rotate, so ask for the current local selection.

Name: Yardleys Taproom
Location: G/F, 62 Peel Street, Soho, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Soho taproom of local brewery Yardley Brothers, pouring its own beers on Peel Street. Why: A brewery-owned local craft room in Soho, near the Mid-Levels Escalator and the market end of Graham Street.

Name: Sun Hing Restaurant (Kennedy Town)
Location: Shop C, G/F, 8 Sze Mei Road, Kennedy Town, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Dim sum house that opens at 03:00 and serves until 16:00; the custard 'liu sha' bun, curry tripe, shrimp dumplings and crab-roe siu mai are the draws. Why: The classic overnight 'night tea' stop for the post-club crowd and early shift workers, per HK01's May 2026 supper roundup. An after-midnight meal on 26 or 27 Dec before sunrise at the Kennedy Town promenade.

Name: Miu Kai Siu Sik (Temple Street skewers and satay noodles)
Location: Shop 5, Wing Sing Lane, Yau Ma Tei, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Charcoal-grilled skewers (squid, pork neck, chicken kidney) and satay beef noodles, open 18:00 to 03:00, next to the Temple Street night market. Why: A lively after-dinner supper stop in Yau Ma Tei; named in HK01's May 2026 supper guide, so useful after Temple Street or the fruit market.

Name: Tai Lung Fung
Location: 5 Hing Wan Street, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A small neighbourhood bar styled as a loving mock-up of mid-century Hong Kong, with iron lamps, old film posters, yellowed newspaper clippings and retro board games. Cocktails lean local (lemongrass martini, plum wine) alongside Hong Kong-style bar snacks. Why: Named after a famous 1960s Cantonese opera troupe (a name now shorthand for gaudy kitsch), it is the best-known retro-pastiche bar in Wan Chai and sits steps from the Blue House cluster and Lee Tung Avenue.

Name: BOUND by Hillywood
Location: 32 Boundary Street, Prince Edward, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A film-and-music-minded coffee and cocktail bar on Boundary Street, with neon-lit retro decor, vinyl, film-themed collaboration cocktails, a daily limited banoffee pie and occasional pop-up markets and screenings. Why: Boundary Street was the old colonial border between Kowloon and the New Territories; Bound is a young-local hangout in that old tong lau strip, with ties to the M+ Cinema and cult-film crowd.

Name: Halfway Coffee
Location: 26 Upper Lascar Row (Cat Street), Sheung Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A tiny retro café on the antiques lane of Cat Street where hot drinks are served in mismatched vintage Chinese porcelain cups from the owner's collection of hundreds. Rose latte and black sugar latte are the usual orders. Why: It is a sit-down break in the middle of the Cat Street / Hollywood Road antiques crawl, and the old porcelain cups make it a distinctly Hong Kong take on specialty coffee.

Name: Quinary
Location: G/F, 56-58 Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A Central cocktail bar known for liquid-nitrogen and molecular techniques, such as its signature Earl Grey caviar martini and spherified creations, in a bright, laboratory-style room. Why: Long a pioneer of Hong Kong's modernist cocktail scene on Hollywood Road, a short walk from SoHo and Man Mo Temple.

Name: Penicillin
Location: L/G, Amber Lodge, 23 Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A closed-loop sustainable cocktail bar that ferments, pickles and distils its own ingredients, built around zero-waste cocktails and house-made sodas and tinctures. Why: Hong Kong's first closed-loop sustainable bar, which regularly features in Asia's 50 Best Bars and was No. 69 on the World's 50 Best Bars 2026 (51-100 list).

Name: Knutsford Terrace
Location: Knutsford Terrace (pedestrian lane off Kimberley Road, behind Miramar Shopping Centre), Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A pedestrian lane of 30-plus bars and restaurants with outdoor tables, from casual pubs and sports bars to cocktail spots, usually with drinks about HK$150-400. Why: Kowloon's Lan Kwai Fong, with cheaper prices and a more relaxed crowd than Central, a handy post-dinner stop for TST visitors.

Name: Lockhart Road bars, Wan Chai
Location: Lockhart Road (between Fenwick Street and Luard Road), Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Wan Chai's long-running bar strip, with Irish and sports pubs (Delaney's, Carnegie's, Coyote), live-music and neon-lit older bars, and a few remnants of the district's Suzie Wong sailor-bar history; Joe Bananas on Luard Road is a late-night institution. Why: Hong Kong's old red-light-turned-pub district, a lively, no-frills night out that stays open later than SoHo or LKF.
